Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

npmatch (development version)

Name normalization

  • 16 more abbreviations expand, taken from networked990’s 990 name resolver and checked against the BMF: FDN / FND / FNDTN / FDTN (FOUNDATION), HOSP, MED, HLTH, HLTHCARE, MGMT, REG / RGNL (REGIONAL), CNTR, SYS / SYST and SRVCS / SRVS. PHYS is deliberately left alone (in the BMF it is mostly physical education). Because this changes name_key, it can change which EINs stage 1 matches, and np_normalize_signature() changes with it.
  • np_normalize() adds name_core, an exact-lookup key that drops connector words and legal forms anywhere in the name but keeps FOUNDATION, TRUST and FUND, so a charity and its foundation get different keys. np_name_core() computes it for raw strings.
  • np_normalize() adds name_placeholder, TRUE for names that are not names (“SEE SCHEDULE O”, “N/A”, no letters). np_block() gives such query rows no candidates. np_name_placeholder() checks raw strings.
  • np_name_rules() returns the normalization tables, for porting the rules to another engine such as a DuckDB SQL macro.

npmatch 0.1.0 (v0)

First tagged release (git tag v0.1.0). It pins the code that produced the combined 2025NOV + 2026MAY SAM-to-BMF crosswalk, so that crosswalk can be reproduced and cited against a fixed version of the package.

Results of the pinned run

Of 175,053 SAM nonprofit registrants, 141,420 (80.8%) are matched to an IRS BMF EIN:

matched by matches share of matches
stage 1 — probabilistic cascade 121,972 86.2%
stage 2 — LLM adjudication of MAYBEs 12,443 8.8%
stage 3 — LLM research of NOs 7,005 5.0%

The 33,633 unmatched registrants are mostly explained by stage 3: 12,892 are not nonprofits, 18,770 are nonprofits absent from this BMF vintage (mostly churches and foreign organizations), and 1,971 could not be determined.

What is in this release

Matching engine

  • A full record-linkage pipeline against the BMF: np_query() / np_reference() → np_normalize() → np_block() → np_compare() → np_score() → np_veto() → np_select() → np_tier() → np_route(), orchestrated by np_cascade() (multi-pass) or np_match() (single pass).
  • Nonprofit-specific normalization: abbreviation expansion, legal-suffix stripping, legal-form capture, and extraction of embedded numbers, ordinals and directions. np_normalize_signature() lets a cached artifact detect when normalization has drifted.
  • Progressive blocking passes: four exact name/DBA passes, then IDF-weighted name-token blocking within a state, a de-spaced-compound pass, and a cross-state pass. np_ref_index() tokenizes the reference once for reuse across passes and batches.
  • Hierarchical scoring (method = "hier"): name similarity plus the strongest confirmed geographic granularity, with a state-aware promotion for rare exact names.
  • A do-not-match veto engine (np_default_rules()): hard vetoes for number, ordinal and direction conflicts and for-profit legal forms; soft vetoes (cap at MAYBE) for affiliate-suffix mismatches and government entities.
  • YES / MAYBE / NO tiering with a near-tie margin and soft-veto demotion.

Running a project

  • Per-run project scaffolding: np_project_init(), np_project_use(), np_project_path() and np_project_status().
  • Stage drivers that share one outcome schema (np_stage_schema()): np_stage1_run() (batched cascade via np_run_batches()), np_stage2_run() (MAYBE adjudication hand-off), np_stage3_run() (NO research, with the np_entity_gate() screen) and np_final_run() (crosswalk, evaluation frame and funnel report).
  • np_merge_decisions() joins stage-2 adjudications back onto the review frame.

Review, labeling and training

  • Candidate-level review frames and LLM prompts: np_route(), np_as_prompt() / np_as_prompts(), np_review_report() (static HTML review report), np_label_frame(), np_calibration_frame() and np_veto_audit().
  • Model fitting and evaluation: np_train(), np_benchmark(), np_auc(), np_evaluate() and np_tune_thresholds().
  • Bundled data: npmatch_eval and npmatch_groundtruth, a hand-labeled 1,502-organization benchmark.

Data management

  • A data store with a manifest (np_data_init(), np_manifest()), source fetchers for the BMF and SAM extracts (np_fetch_bmf(), np_fetch_sam(), np_prepare_sam()), incremental diffs (np_diff_unmatched()) and run reports (np_run_report()).
  • Geography helpers: city aliases, HUD crosswalks, RUCA urbanicity and ZIP lookups.

Documentation

  • Articles: Workflow, Reviewer guide, Candidate evaluation frame, Training dataset and Building a classifier, published with the pkgdown site.
  • Reviewer workbook builds under dev/review-workbooks/: per-state themed evaluation workbooks, plus the stage-3 secondary review workbooks (all states, per state and zipped).

Known issues

  • Blocking misses. Of the 4,925 stage-3 matches that stage 1 never surfaced, 3,189 were never generated by blocking, 1,507 were scored but missed the shortlist, and 229 were hard-vetoed. final_ein_in_candset = 0 therefore mixes blocking, scoring and veto misses rather than marking blocking failures alone; the stage-3 secondary review separates them in stage1_pair_status.
  • Word-order sensitivity. Name similarity is Jaro-Winkler on the normalized name, so a reordered name (e.g. “BERNARDINO TELACU HOUSING SAN II” vs “TELACU HOUSING SAN BERNARDINO II”) can fall below the 0.85 floor. The order-insensitive overlap recovery only runs when the address already matches.
  • Fully vetoed registrants. For 5,226 registrants, stage 1 scored candidate pairs but the hard veto removed every one. They are flagged fully_vetoed in the secondary review for inspection. Among the 229 vetoed stage-3 matches, the for-profit legal-form rule accounts for 183.
  • Rollup anomaly. 126 stage3_research rows in the combined evaluation frame are NO_MATCH with an EIN but a blank final_ein; synthetic rows should only exist for matched registrants.
  • candidate_source = "none" rows come from the combined-run build, which is not part of the package; that value is not yet documented in the reviewer data dictionary.
